title: The 1908 ‘first cartoon’ looks chalked on a blackboard but was drawn on paper

cover.alt: White line drawing on a black background: a stick-figure clown lying back along the long trunk of a cartoon elephant.

body: Émile Cohl’s *Fantasmagorie*, released on 17 August 1908, is considered by film historians to be the first animated cartoon. Cohl drew each frame on paper and then shot it onto **negative film**, which reverses light and dark, so his lines came out pale on black and gave the film its blackboard look. He made **700 drawings** and exposed each one twice, which animators call working ‘on twos’. He worked on it from February to May or June 1908.

slides.alt: White-line animation on black: a stick-figure clown meets a bottle and climbs inside it, the bottle opens into a flower, and the flower’s stem turns into an elephant’s trunk.
slides.caption: In Fantasmagorie, a clown climbs into a bottle that opens into a flower, and the flower’s stem becomes an elephant’s trunk.
slides.music: “Fig Leaf Rag” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.question: How many drawings did Émile Cohl make for Fantasmagorie?
slides.explanation: 700, each one exposed twice. The live-action hands of the animator also appear in the film, drawing the main character.

slides.heading: How Cohl got the blackboard look
One copy left
slides.text: Fantasmagorie’s master negative is presumed lost, perhaps to nitrate decay, neglect or the recovery of silver from old film. The only surviving full-frame copy is a 16 mm print, tracked down for the film’s 100th anniversary in 2008 and now held by the Academy Film Archive.

slides.question: The title comes from a 19th-century show. What did a phantasmagoria show?
slides.explanation: A phantasmagoria was a magic lantern show with moving images of ghosts. Cohl’s ever-changing shapes were also a tribute to the Incoherents, a forgotten art movement.
